content.value: Primary reading: Rozanski and Woods, Chapters 14 and 30. Supplemental: SEI ATAM and Views and Beyond. This unit focuses on communicating architecture.

Architecture communication adapts to audience. Executives need risks, options, cost, and business impact. Developers need boundaries, interfaces, decisions, and constraints. Operators need deployment, monitoring, recovery, and ownership.
The architect acts as a translator across concerns. Effective communication uses the smallest set of views and narratives that help stakeholders make better decisions.
Studio: prepare a five-minute architecture briefing for a non-technical sponsor and a separate five-minute briefing for an implementation team.

concepts.name: Architecture narrative
concepts.description: A coherent explanation of the system context, major decisions, tradeoffs, risks, and consequences.

concepts.name: Audience adaptation
concepts.description: Changing architecture communication to match stakeholder knowledge, decisions, and concerns.

concepts.name: Architecture briefing
concepts.description: A concise presentation or walkthrough of architecture information for a particular audience.

concepts.name: Decision framing
concepts.description: Presenting architectural choices in terms of options, consequences, evidence, and stakeholder impact.
